faqSection.subtitle: From Seed Ball Technology to release by drone, from the certificate to reporting — the questions people ask.

seedBall.question: What is Seed Ball Technology and how does it work?
seedBall.answer: Seed Ball Technology is a method in which native seeds are encapsulated in clay and organic nutrients, protecting them from external factors and raising germination success above 65%+. The capsule shields the seed from drought and from being eaten; it dissolves with rainfall and the seed germinates in its natural cycle.

sourcing.question: Where are the seeds sourced from?
sourcing.answer: All seeds are sourced in cooperation with the Regional Forestry Directorates. In line with the principles of preserving biodiversity and sustainability, the collection date, genetic origin, and taxonomic (species) information of every seed lot is recorded using blockchain technology. Thanks to our end-to-end transparent supply chain, our customers can access seed ID cards and certification data at any time.

droneEfficiency.question: How efficient is seed ball release by drone?
droneEfficiency.answer: By releasing more than 200 seed balls in a single flight, it is 10 times faster than traditional methods and highly cost-effective. GPS-precise coordinates make it possible to reach steep and fire-affected areas that people cannot access, and because no one enters the land, soil and vegetation are protected.

tracking.question: How can I follow the development of the released seed balls?
tracking.answer: Sites are re-surveyed by drone every year. About six months after the release we publish footage of the work as a public video and send you the link by email. For organisations, the results are also compiled in the Activity Report.

certificate.question: What is the Certificate of Participation?
certificate.answer: After the seed balls have been released on the site, we email you a Certificate of Participation. It shows the name you chose, the site, the date and the number of seed balls, and you can share it on social media. The certificate is not a donation receipt and does not provide any tax deduction.

minOrder.question: What is the minimum number of seed balls?
minOrder.answer: You can take part with a minimum of 20 seed balls. You can use one of the preset options or set the quantity yourself; the current fee is shown on the site page and at the order step.

b2bIntegration.question: How does B2B corporate integration work?
b2bIntegration.answer: Our corporate panel includes modules such as employee list upload, automatic PDF certificate generation, an e-commerce "add seeds to cart" integration, and an ESG reporting API. A dedicated account manager is assigned and customization is carried out according to the organization's needs.

gift.question: Can I send it as a gift?
gift.answer: Yes. You decide which name appears on the certificate, so you can enter the name of someone you care about and give them the Certificate of Participation as a gift.

species.question: Do I choose which species is released?
species.answer: No. The species is determined by our specialists according to the site's climate, soil and natural vegetation. On each site's page you can see which species is released and why.

calendar.question: When are the seed balls released?
calendar.answer: Release work takes place between October and March — the best period for the seed to meet rainfall. From April to September the sites are inspected, monitored and reported on. About six months after the release we share footage of the work.

hectare.question: What is a hectare?
hectare.answer: A hectare is a unit of area: 1 hectare is 10,000 square metres (about 2.47 acres) — roughly one and a half football pitches. We state the size of our sites in hectares.

carbonReport.question: Can I obtain a carbon report or carbon credits through this work?
carbonReport.answer: No. The document we provide is an Activity Report: it records the site, area, species, date, coordinates and footage of the work. It is not a carbon credit or a carbon-neutral certificate; it cannot be deducted from your greenhouse gas inventory or used for offsetting. Carbon uptake on the sites has not been calculated and verified by an independent body to date. If such a verification is carried out, we will publish it here together with its method and results.

notDonation.question: Is this a donation?
notDonation.answer: No. What you buy from Skytech Green is a service: the release by drone of the number of seed balls you choose on the site you select. An invoice is issued for the service fee; your payment is not a donation and does not provide any tax deduction.

meta.title: Carbon & Reporting — The Activity Report
meta.description: For every job we issue an Activity Report covering site, area, species, date, coordinates and footage — and we say plainly what the report is for and what it is not.

schema.name: Activity Report and Monitoring
schema.description: An Activity Report covering site, area, species, date, coordinates and footage for seed ball release by drone, together with annual monitoring.

hero.title: Carbon & Reporting
hero.subtitle: We document the work we do, and we do not promise what we cannot document. Here is what the Activity Report is — and what it is not.

report.subtitle: We issue an Activity Report for every site where seed balls are released. It contains:

site.title: Site and location
site.desc: The Project Site where the work took place, with its province and district.

area.title: Area
area.desc: The size of the area worked on, in hectares.

species.title: Species and seed source
species.desc: The species released on the site and where the seed was sourced.

date.title: Date and flight log
date.desc: The date of the release and the records of the drone flights.

coordinates.title: Coordinates
coordinates.desc: The coordinates of the area where the seed balls were released.

footage.title: Footage and monitoring
footage.desc: Drone footage taken during the work and in the monitoring period, plus the annual monitoring results.

can.heading: How you can use it
items: As supporting evidence in the nature, biodiversity and social-contribution sections of your sustainability report
As a concrete record of the work in your internal and external communications
As the basis for the Certificates of Participation you share with employees and stakeholders
To follow how the site develops over the years

cannot.heading: What it is not
items: It is not a carbon credit or a carbon-neutral certificate
It cannot be deducted from your greenhouse gas inventory or used for offsetting
It is not a donation receipt and provides no tax deduction
It does not guarantee germination or a number of trees; the path from seed to tree takes years and depends on natural conditions

why.body: Forests store carbon — but stating how much carbon a given piece of work has stored requires years of measurement and independent verification. Carbon uptake on our sites has not been calculated and verified by an independent body to date. That is why we give no figures and make no claims such as carbon neutrality.
points: A corporate greenhouse gas inventory covers the organisation's own operational boundary; forest work carried out by a third party cannot be deducted from it.
Carbon credits are generated at project level, through a registered project, independent validation and periodic measurement. A single order does not produce credits.
If an independent verification is carried out, we will publish its scope, method and results on this page.

credit.question: Can I obtain a carbon report or carbon credits through this work?
credit.answer: No. The document we provide is an Activity Report: it records the site, area, species, date, coordinates and footage of the work. It is not a carbon credit or a carbon-neutral certificate; it cannot be deducted from your greenhouse gas inventory or used for offsetting.

sustainability.question: How do I use the Activity Report in my sustainability report?
sustainability.answer: You can include it as evidence of the work you supported under nature, biodiversity and social contribution. Do not report it as an emission reduction or removal; such statements require verified carbon credits.

individual.question: Can I take part as an individual?
individual.answer: Yes. You can choose a Project Site and have seed balls released there. After the release you receive your Certificate of Participation by email, and about six months later the footage of the work.

future.question: Will there be a carbon verification in the future?
future.answer: That is a process requiring project-level registration and long-term measurement. If such a step is taken we will share its scope, method and results here openly; until then we make no statement about carbon quantities.
